article_content: TAV Havalimanlari Holding A.S. (TAVHY) experienced a significant drop in short interest during October, sparking concerns among investors. As of October 15th, short interest had plummeted to 1,000 shares, a drastic 30% decrease from the September 30th total of 1,500 shares. This sudden shift has raised eyebrows in the financial community. Based on an average daily volume of 900 shares, the short-interest ratio now stands at just 1.1 days. The stock opened at $17.82 on Friday, with a 50-day moving average of $17.83 and a 200-day moving average of $16.43. TAVHY's 12-month performance shows a low of $12.06 and a high of $20.92. The company, a perceived leader in global airport management, operates across multiple countries, including recent expansions into China and India, and has stepped up its efforts in terminal constructions and duty-free operations.
